p005-u001: The RoboMaster University Series (RMU), initiated by DJI, is one of the events under the National College Student Robot Competition and is a robot competition and academic exchange platform created for technology enthusiasts worldwide. Since its founding in 2013, it has upheld the philosophy of ‘giving glory to youth, giving thinking its power, and serving young engineers worldwide in becoming dreamers who pursue excellence and are action-oriented’. It is committed to cultivating and attracting well-rounded talents with an engineering mindset, while spreading the beauty of technology and the idea of technological innovation widely to the public.
p005-u002: The National College Student Robot Competition RoboMaster University Championship (RMUC) focuses on participants’ comprehensive application of science and engineering disciplines and their engineering practice ability, fully integrating many robot-related technical disciplines such as ‘mechanical engineering’,
p005-u003: ‘embedded system design’, ‘control algorithms’, ‘electrical engineering’, ‘integrated communication and sensing’, ‘autonomous navigation’ and ‘human-machine interaction’. It also innovatively combines popular presentation styles with robot competition, making robot confrontation more intuitive and intense and attracting the wide attention of technology enthusiasts and the general public.
p005-u004: The National College Student Robot Competition RoboMaster University League (RMUL) is bid for by local academic institutions and universities and draws in surrounding universities to participate. It aims to promote regional exchange of university robotics technology, foster a strong academic atmosphere, and support regional scientific and technological innovation and development.
p005-u005: RMUL offers two challenge events: the 3V3 Match and the Infantry Match.

p026-u001: All RoboMaster participants must fully understand that safety is the most important prerequisite for the continued development of the competition. To protect the rights and interests of all participants and event organizers, and in accordance with relevant laws and regulations, by registering for RoboMaster, all participants acknowledge and agree to abide by the following safety terms:
p026-u003: All participants must have full capacity for civil conduct and the ability to independently build and operate robots. Before building robots with products of the event organizer, SZ DJI Technology Co., Ltd., they must carefully read the registration notice, competition rules and other relevant documents.
p026-u005: During the event, ensure that building, testing and using robots will not harm one’s own team members, opposing team members, referees, staff, spectators, equipment or the competition venue.
p026-u007: Ensure that the robot’s structural design allows convenient safety inspection during Pre-Match Inspection, and actively cooperate with the event organizer’s Pre-Match Inspection.
p026-u009: The use of fuel-powered engines, explosives or hazardous chemical materials is prohibited. Hydraulic or other power methods that may cause pollution are also prohibited.
p026-u011: At any stage of R&D, preparation and participation, team members must pay full attention to safety and comply with the RoboMaster University Series Battery Safety Specifications; advisors should take responsibility for safety guidance and supervision.
p026-u013: Ensure the robots are safe and their launching mechanisms are in a safe state, so that they never directly or indirectly injure participants, referees, staff or spectators.
p026-u015: During R&D, training and participation, take sufficient and necessary safety measures against possible accidents, such as wearing safety goggles.
p026-u016: Avoid loss of control of the control system. Urge team members to think through operating steps beforehand to prevent mistakes and collisions between team members or between team members and robots. Team members must not train alone; ensure someone can respond to accidents in an emergency. During debugging, add appropriate safety measures to the robot system, such as proper locking and emergency stop switches.
p026-u018: The participating team that caused an accident is solely responsible for all accident liability and corresponding losses arising during practice or competition from unexpected situations such as robot failure or loss of control of an unmanned aerial vehicle in flight.
p026-u020: All participating teams must strictly comply with local laws and regulations on flight control. A team’s Aerial Robot flying above the competition field in a specific restricted area of the venue is an indoor flight and does not require airspace approval. To ensure flight safety, the Aerial Robot is connected by a rope to a ground anchor. If an unexpected situation occurs, such as the Aerial Robot breaking free of its safety tether, the pilot must land it and stop its propellers as soon as possible; continued flight is strictly prohibited. Participating teams’ Aerial Robots must not fly outdoors.
p026-u021: Items sold or provided by the event organizer, SZ DJI Technology Co., Ltd., such as batteries and the Referee System, must be used according to their instructions. SZ DJI Technology Co., Ltd. is not liable for injury caused by improper use. The participating team is responsible for bodily injury or property damage to itself or any third party caused by building or operating its robot.
